# OX — Frontend Design Sets, Generated by Agents

A single-page showcase that hosts **sets of five frontend designs**, each set built around the ox. Every design is a complete art direction of its own — palette, typography, (AI)hand-drawn SVG artwork and motion language — switchable at runtime without reloading.

This project is focused on **frontend designs generated by agents**: every layout, illustration, color system and animation was authored end-to-end by an AI agent as a demonstration of machine-driven design craft.

## The sets

> **Curation note (2026-09-04):** this showcase was reviewed end-to-end and cut to the sets that pass the ox gate — every design is judged on its rendered page by one question, *does the image portray a bovine in any form, and does it resemble one?* — and a set passes at **4 of 5 designs or better**. Ten sets failed and were removed; three more (OX BIOMES, OX SIGNALS, OX GLYPHS) passed that review but failed a manual re-grade of the rendered pages later the same day and were removed too. The full review lives in [docs/gallery/SCORECARD.md](docs/gallery/SCORECARD.md), the passing sets are ranked in [docs/gallery/LEADERBOARD.md](docs/gallery/LEADERBOARD.md), and every removal is recorded in [docs/gallery/WALLOFSHAME.md](docs/gallery/WALLOFSHAME.md).

> **Second audit (2026-09-11):** the whole gallery was re-rendered and re-graded against the same gate. OX ARENA, the first review's runner-up, failed it at 1 of 5 recognizable oxen — the Minoan bull reads as a leaping hare, the rodeo bull as a bronco — and was removed. The survivors were re-scored in the same pass; the current ranking lives in [docs/gallery/LEADERBOARD.md](docs/gallery/LEADERBOARD.md).

> **Manual pass (2026-09-11, maintainer):** the maintainer re-graded the surviving sets by eye, as after the first review. OX SENSORIUM failed it: the ox figures were judged unacceptable and unrecognizable as animals, and the set was removed. Every removal is recorded in [docs/gallery/WALLOFSHAME.md](docs/gallery/WALLOFSHAME.md).

## Switching designs and sets

The bottom-right cluster controls everything:

- **Design dock** — five color chips switch designs within the active set (keys `1`–`5`)
- **Set bar** — `‹` / `›` cycle between sets; clicking the set name opens the **set manager**
- **Set manager modal** — browse all sets as cards, View / Hide any set, and pick which set loads at startup ("Start here")

Keyboard: `1`–`5` designs · `[` / `]` cycle sets · `Esc` closes the modal.

Choices persist locally: the last-viewed design per set, hidden sets, and your chosen startup set are remembered in `localStorage`.

## Architecture

Built to scale horizontally — a set is just a folder:

```
src/showcase/
├── ShowcaseContext.jsx        # state: active set/design, hidden sets, default set + persistence
└── sets/
    ├── index.js               # REGISTRY — one line per set
    ├── ox-vesper/
    │   ├── manifest.js        # { id, name, tagline, accent, credit, designs: [...] }
    │   └── (5 components + css)
    └── ox-atlas/
        └── ...
```

- Each design is registered in its set's `manifest.js` as a `React.lazy` import, so **every design ships as its own chunk** and the initial bundle stays small.
- Adding a new set of five = create a folder with a manifest + register one line in `sets/index.js`. Nothing else changes.
- Designs mount through `Suspense` inside the transition wrapper, keyed by `${setId}:${designId}`, with crossfade transitions on both switches.

## Tech stack

- [Vite](https://vitejs.dev/) + [React](https://react.dev/)
- [Framer Motion](https://www.framer.com/motion/) for springs, scroll reveals and crossfade transitions
- [Playwright](https://playwright.dev/) for end-to-end testing
- Hand-written CSS per design (no UI framework) + inline SVG artwork drawn in code
- Google Fonts

## Run it

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

Then open the printed local URL. Production build:

```bash
npm run build
npm run preview
```

## Testing (Playwright)

[Playwright](https://playwright.dev/) drives a real Chromium browser against the dev server (started automatically by the config). End-to-end specs live in `tests/`.

```bash
npm test              # run all specs headless
npm run test:ui       # run with the Playwright UI mode
npx playwright install chromium   # (re)install the browser binary if needed
```

The runner config is `playwright.config.js`: Chromium, `baseURL` `http://localhost:5173`, and a `webServer` hook that boots `npm run dev` (reusing an already-running dev server outside CI). Specs match `tests/*.spec.js`; the bundled smoke test checks that the app mounts and renders a design heading. Traces are captured on first retry; run `npx playwright show-report` after a CI run to inspect the HTML report.


## Prompt used

You are contributing one set of five frontend designs to the OX showcase. The stack is Vite + React + Framer Motion. The subject is fixed: the ox. Every design must show a bovine that a stranger can name on sight.

Read AGENTS.md in full before you propose anything. It owns the rules. These three decide whether your set gets in:

1. The ox gate. Each design is judged on the rendered page by one question: does the image portray a bovine in any form, and does it resemble one? At least 4 of 5 must pass or the whole set fails, no matter how good the rest looks. Check every design yourself before you commit. A caption or a label is not the animal.
2. Five different pages. Different palette, type, layout, and motion. If two of your designs could swap CSS variables and still work, redesign one.
3. Sign your work three ways, as the brief describes. No signature, no attribution, no pass.

Do not mine the other sets for ideas. You may read one manifest.js to learn how a set is wired; everything else in their folders stays closed. Draw your own ox, path by path. Their themes are fair game.

Propose your five facets in one message before you write any SVG: name each facet, and describe the figure you will draw for it (where the horns sit, how many legs show, what the silhouette reads as from the viewer's angle). Then build, run npm run build, and render every design at 1440px and 375px before you call it done.
